summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of stroke, presented with asymptomatic hypotension during dialysis. Initial arm blood pressure readings were in the 50s, but repeat measurements on the thigh showed normal values in the 90s to 120s, suggesting spurious hypotension. He had no signs of infection, and blood cultures showed no growth. Labs improved with fluids and dialysis. He was continued on midodrine and monitored for stability. Pressure ulcers on the sacrum, right elbow, and left heel were noted, and home nursing was arranged for wound care. Weight loss was attributed to poor oral intake, and outpatient colonoscopy was recommended. He remained alert and stable, with discharge to home with services and follow-up plans.
